## Activity

Oakridge Primary Care recorded 85 captures during July 2025. This represents the total capture activity reported for the month. The activity provides the basis for subsequent image-quality review and grading. Records should continue to be reviewed as part of routine site monitoring so that changes in activity can be identified and followed up through normal operational processes.

## Image quality

Image-quality review found that 4 captures were ungradable. The ungradable rate was 4.7 per cent. These captures could not be used for grading and should be considered when reviewing the overall quality of the site’s activity. Ongoing attention to capture practice and equipment performance will support the production of images suitable for assessment.

## Grading

Grading identified 12 referable captures. The median lag between capture and grading was 1 day. This indicates that the reported activity was processed within a short interval overall, although individual cases may have varied. The site should continue to monitor grading outcomes, image quality and processing times through routine reporting, with any recurring operational issues managed through established local arrangements.
